confirmedChecks: The high-level sequence is coherent: PIN-01—06 initials; PIN-07—13 finals; PIN-14—16 syllable construction and whole-syllable recognition; PIN-17 spelling; PIN-18 tones; PIN-19 synthesis.
PIN-05 and PIN-16 must agree on zi/ci/si and the 16 whole-syllable-recognition syllables.
PIN-10/PIN-12/PIN-17 must use consistent ü and spelling-rule explanations.
PIN-14/PIN-15 must distinguish two-part from three-part syllables; miàn is m + i + an.
PIN-16/PIN-17 must align the 16 whole-syllable-recognition set with spelling rules.
PIN-18/PIN-19 must distinguish tone-rule demonstration examples from Atlas vocabulary.
PIN-19 must use Atlas source pinyin 睡觉 shuì jiào and treat each syllable in 火锅 huǒ guō as an initial-plus-final (two-part) syllable.

Revised syllable-structure audit distinguishes 192 source syllable occurrences, 122 distinct tone-stripped spellings, zero-initial y/w orthography, j/q/x + u -> ü, iu/ui/un abbreviations, apical i, and candidate medial structures.
Atlas intersects 13 of the conventional 16 whole-syllable-recognition types, across 31 occurrences; see atlas-phonetic-coverage.json for exact source positions.

The 10 forms previously labelled extended finals have been reclassified in the audit as medial-bearing compound-final forms / orthographic patterns; this avoids implying ten extra basic finals or a confirmed curriculum gap.

A dedicated PIN-17 Atlas spelling-rule matrix now maps iu→iou (5 occurrences), ui→uei (3), written un (4), j/q/x + u-family→ü-family (5), zero-initial y/w spellings (21), and apical i after z/c/s/zh/ch/sh/r (19); course-text teaching remains unverified.
